thread:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal for a lightweight runtime shim to smooth differences between Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments. Posting a rough sketch and tradeoffs.

maria: Motivation: customers expect the same API/behaviors but Private has strict network/KMS/egress rules and Dedicated has reserved capacity. We need a minimal boundary so control-plane code doesn't special-case each mode. :thinking:

maria: Sketch of the shim (pseudo):
```
interface DeploymentShim {
  serve(request: InferenceRequest): InferenceResponse
  health(): HealthStatus
  metrics(): MetricsSnapshot
  config(): RuntimeConfig
}
// Implementations: HostedShim (proxy->rls), DedicatedShim (local pool), PrivateShim (edge agent + KMS)
```

kevin: LGTM overall. A couple quick concerns: auth & KMS surface — Private should enforce KMS locally and not leak keys to control plane. How do we keep the shim API generic but let impls enforce stronger constraints?

maria: plan is to keep policy enforcement inside the impls. shim only conveys intent (e.g., `encrypt: boolean`, `kms_key_id: string | null`) and the PrivateShim rejects/enforces based on local policy. control-plane never sees plaintext keys.

anya: What about observability? We currently rely on centralized traces/metrics in Hosted. Private customers might block telemetry egress. We need a pluggable metrics sink with an opt-in forwarder.

maria: agreed. shim exposes `metrics()` and `traces()` hooks. Implementations can write to an internal buffer and ship if allowed, or write to a customer-hosted collector. We'll document the contract: eventual consistency, no PII in metrics by default.

devon: Another tradeoff: latency vs feature parity. Dedicated pools allow lower latency but different batching behavior. Do we accept small API differences like `batching_hint` tolerated?

kevin: I'd prefer surfacing hints rather than behavior changes. e.g., `batching_hint: \"prefer-low-latency\"` vs `\"max-throughput\"`. shim impls decide exact scheduling but must respect semantic SLOs.

anya: Rollout/migrations: we should support versioned shim contracts so older control-plane versions still work. Recommend a numeric `shim_version` on the handshake and a compatibility matrix in the config.

maria: +1. Also thinking about testing: add a `local-test-shim` that simulates Private restrictions (no egress, local KMS stub) so dev teams can run full integration tests.

devon: How do we handle fallbacks? If Dedicated pool is saturated, Hosted fallback should be possible for customers who allow it. The shim should include `capacity_policy` and a `fallback_allowed` flag.

maria: yep — shim handshake includes `capacity_policy: { prefer: dedicated|hosted|private, fallback: boolean }`. Control-plane uses that to route, but the runtime can choose to decline and return `RETRY_WITHOUT_FALLBACK`.

kevin: Security note: for PrivateShim we must mute any debug endpoints and audit all `config()` reads. Might require an HSM-backed attestation from the runtime.

maria: noted. add `attestation_token` optional field produced by runtime for sensitive ops.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new branch `runtime/shim-v1` has CI passing. Integration test includes Hosted <-> Private shim handshake simulation. See: https://ci.redwood.company/1234 :rocket:

anya: Next steps I suggest: 1) formalize shim proto, 2) implement LocalTestShim, 3) add a Minimal PrivateShim that handles KMS + no-egress, 4) bake compatibility matrix. Anyone object?

kevin: No objections. can I take task 1 and 4?

maria: assigning to @kevin for the proto and matrix. @devon please take LocalTestShim. I'll pair with anya on PrivateShim acceptance criteria.

devon: on it. will open a short RFC PR with the proto within the day.

maria: thanks everyone. keeping this small and explicit should avoid a billion special-cases. :thumbsup:
